goal: Make the post-payment thank-you advertise every other currently available SummonScout destination across the live fallback-router fleet, excluding this client's own service and failing safe to thank-only when no verified other route is available.
notes: Primary post-payment copy now derives other routes from fallbackrouter.directory plus live fallbackrouter.providers using the existing 38s provider TTL, excludes every locally configured service id, and formats one/two/many destination labels. Primary exports a narrow message builder/detector so PostPaymentFallbackHot uses the same dynamic route list and cannot duplicate a valid dynamic thank-you. If the fleet directory is unavailable or has no other route, both paths send thank-only rather than advertising an unverified location.
